Alexandre Dumas, The Wolf-Leader, translated by Alfred Allinson.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/alexandre-dumas/the-wolf-leader/alfred-allinson

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Alexandre Dumas, the author, died 1870 (Wikidata Q38337, P570 1870-12-05).
- Alfred Allinson, the translator and annotator, died 1929 (Wikidata Q4723343, P570 1929-12-01).

First publication of the text used: 1904, the English translation by Alfred Allinson. The French original was published in 1857. The country of first publication of the translation is not stated in the facts. (SE colophon: 'The Wolf-Leader was published in 1857 by Alexandre Dumas. It was translated from French in 1904 by Alfred Allinson.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the translation was first published in 1904 and the original in 1857, both before 1931, so the text is in the United States public domain. The edition's rights statement quoted below says the same.
- Country of origin: Two layers, checked separately. Original: French work by Alexandre Dumas (died 1870), first published 1857. The author died before 1926, so the original is public domain in every country. Translation (English): the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each has a term of life + 70 years or less. The translator Alfred Allinson (died 1929) left the public domain in each of them on 1 January 2000, so the translation is public domain in each. The country of first publication therefore makes no difference.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
